title: Simulation Task
description: Develop a multi-agent simulation system that models the spread of mask-wearing behavior through social networks.
simulation_focus: Predict agents' mask-wearing behavior over day 30 - day 39 (last ten days) based on their attributes, social connections, and past behavior
Model information propagation and behavioral changes triggered by social influence and government intervention starting on Day 10

data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Contains demographic and behavioral attributes of each agent, including age, occupation, risk perception, and social connection counts
data_files.social_network.json: Contains structured data representing a social network. Each entry corresponds to a user (identified by a unique integer ID), and the values describe the different types of relationships that user has with others. Data Structure: The top-level structure is a dictionary ({} in JSON). Keys: Each key is a unique user ID (as an integer, e.g., 0, 1, 2, etc.). Values: Each value is another dictionary with the following fields: "family": a list of user IDs representing family connections. "work_school": a list of user IDs representing colleagues or schoolmates. "community": a list of user IDs representing community-level acquaintances. "all": a merged list of all user IDs connected to the user across the three categories above.
data_files.train_data.csv: Time series data for the first 30 days, used for training the model

RMSE.description: Root Mean Square Error measuring overall predictive accuracy of mask adoption rates
RMSE.interpretation: Directly interpretable as percentage deviations due to the 0-1 range

Peak Adoption Rate Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting maximum mask adoption during intervention

Time-to-Peak Error.description: Measures model accuracy in predicting the time lag from intervention to peak behavior change

key_patterns.name: Multiplex structure with heterogeneous degrees
key_patterns.description: Community layers have larger neighbor lists, work/school moderate, family smallest. Some edges are non-reciprocal; overlap across layers is possible.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific degree and overlap affect exposure frequency and social reinforcement; informs layer weights and contact sampling.

key_patterns.name: Seeded early adopters
key_patterns.description: initial_mask_wearing provides a non-zero base of adopters at t0 that likely varies by demographics and risk_perception.
key_patterns.relevance: Seeds drive cascade initiation; must be honored to reproduce early dynamics.

key_patterns.name: Risk perception heterogeneity
key_patterns.description: risk_perception is continuous in [0,1] and is expected to correlate positively with adoption propensity.
key_patterns.relevance: Use to modulate thresholds or adoption probabilities; supports heterogeneity in agent susceptibility.

key_patterns.name: Behavioral persistence with asymmetric switching
key_patterns.description: In panel data, wearing_mask tends to persist once adopted; drop-off events occur but are less frequent than adoption (expected).
key_patterns.relevance: Calibrate separate persistence (stickiness) and dropout rates; necessary to match wearing streak-length distributions.

key_patterns.name: Information precedes adoption
key_patterns.description: received_info is a leading indicator for wearing_mask; adoption can occur without received_info but at a lower rate.
key_patterns.relevance: Model two coupled processes (information then behavior) with distinct parameters; estimate uplift from information.

key_patterns.name: Demographic and role structure
key_patterns.description: age_group and occupation align with degree by layer (e.g., students/working-age have more work/school ties).
key_patterns.relevance: Supports homophily and role-constrained wiring; informs contact rates and susceptibility modifiers.

key_patterns.name: Assortativity/homophily
key_patterns.description: Neighbors likely share age_group/occupation more than random; especially within work/school and family.
key_patterns.relevance: Increases local reinforcement; impacts threshold models and cascade sizes.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception
key_distributions.description: Continuous [0,1]; suitable for Beta distribution fit.
key_distributions.parameters: Fit Beta(a,b) to risk_perception from agent_attributes.csv; use method-of-moments or MLE.

key_distributions.name: Degree by layer
key_distributions.description: Right-skewed counts per layer (family < work/school < community). Negative binomial often fits better than Poisson.
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L in {family, work_school, community}: mean_L and dispersion k_L from social_network.json degrees.

key_distributions.name: Initial adoption rate
key_distributions.parameters: p0 = mean(initial_mask_wearing); p0_g by age_group; p0_o by occupation from agent_attributes.csv.

key_distributions.name: Wearing streak lengths
key_distributions.description: Geometric-like distribution for consecutive days wearing; parameterized by dropout probability.
key_distributions.parameters: p_drop = P(wearing_t+1=0 | wearing_t=1); estimate from train_data.csv.

key_distributions.name: Adoption waiting times
key_distributions.description: Time from not-wearing to first wearing; mixture of baseline and info-triggered hazards.
key_distributions.parameters: h_base = P(wearing_t+1=1 | wearing_t=0, received_info_t=0); h_info = P(wearing_t+1=1 | wearing_t=0, received_info_t=1).

key_distributions.name: Information exposure rate
key_distributions.description: Per-day probability of receiving info given neighbor exposures by layer.
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L: p_info_L per contact per day; and p_info_ext for exogenous info; estimated from train_data.csv + social_network.json.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive association; receiving info increases next-day adoption probability.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate odds ratio via logistic regression; expected moderate-to-strong.
High; estimate P(stay wearing) and P(stay not-wearing).

key_relationships.relationship: Positive peer effect with layer heterogeneity (family > work/school > community).
key_relationships.strength: Estimate layer-specific coefficients; expected small-to-moderate per 10% neighbor increase.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher risk_perception correlates with higher adoption.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate marginal effect or interaction with peer influence; expected moderate.

key_relationships.relationship: Role-specific degree patterns (e.g., students/working adults higher work/school degree).
key_relationships.strength: Quantify via mean degree differences and assortativity indices; expected strong.

symmetrize_edges.notes: Undirected influence assumed; keep edge if i->j or j->i.

degree_stats_by_layer.value: Compute empirical mean and dispersion per layer
degree_stats_by_layer.notes: Store mean_L and k_L for contact sampling and sensitivity analyses.

assortativity_by_attribute.notes: Use Newman assortativity; informs homophily strength for any synthetic rewiring.

overlap_across_layers.value: Compute Jaccard overlap of neighbor sets per layer pair per agent

p_info_family.value: Estimate per-contact per-day probability via complementary log-log hazard model

p_info_external.value: Estimate baseline info rate when no informed neighbors
p_info_external.notes: Captures media and other exogenous channels.

info_decay_days.notes: Optional: number of days info remains salient; calibrate if data show waning effect.

update_rule.value: Two-stage daily update: (1) update received_info; (2) update wearing_mask via logistic model

persistence_probability.notes: Controls habit; derive dropout as 1 - P_stay.

dropout_probability.notes: May vary with neighbor behavior and risk_perception; allow dependence if supported.

peer_influence_weights_by_layer.source: Design prior; refine via calibration to match layer-conditional adoption
peer_influence_weights_by_layer.notes: Initial weights; replace with estimated coefficients scaled to sum to 1.

beta_peer_by_layer.value: Estimate logistic coefficients for neighbor_wearing_fraction_family/work_school/community at time t
beta_peer_by_layer.notes: Use lagged neighbor wearing to reduce simultaneity bias.

beta_risk_perception.value: Estimate coefficient for risk_perception in adoption model
beta_risk_perception.notes: Include interaction with peer influence to capture heterogeneous susceptibility.

beta_demographics.value: Estimate effects for age_group and occupation (fixed effects or slopes)
beta_demographics.notes: Controls for role differences; improves out-of-sample fit.

saturation_function.value: Use fractional neighbor wearing with logistic link; cap at [0,1]

initial_mask_seed.value: Use initial_mask_wearing from agent_attributes.csv unless simulating a specific day from train_data.csv
initial_mask_seed.notes: If reproducing observed trajectory from day 0 in train_data.csv, initialize from that day instead.

risk_perception_values.notes: Optionally rescale or transform (e.g., logit) for modeling.

network_state.value: Use social_network.json as fixed multiplex topology

contact_sampling_per_day.source: Design prior; adjust to match info rates
contact_sampling_per_day.notes: Convert adjacency into daily contacts; tune to match observed info hazards.

edge_overlap_reinforcement.value: If the same neighbor is connected in multiple layers, add a reinforcement multiplier to peer influence for that alter
edge_overlap_reinforcement.notes: Calibrate multiplier to match adoption acceleration in dense neighborhoods.

update_order.notes: Prevents same-day simultaneity; use t neighbor states to predict t+1.

preprocessing_steps.step: Convert JSON keys to integers; de-duplicate adjacency lists; enforce undirected edges (symmetrize).
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Ensure consistent node IDs and undirected influence topology.

preprocessing_steps.step: Compute per-layer neighbor sets, degrees, and overlaps; cache for fast exposure calculations.
Validate total_connections equals sum of layer counts; correct or recompute as needed.
Merge agent_attributes.csv into the panel by agent_id; align earliest day as t0.
Construct lagged neighbor summaries per layer per day: fraction_wearing_t, fraction_info_t.
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Create exposure variables for hazard models; mitigate simultaneity by using lagged states.

preprocessing_steps.step: Handle missing days/states via explicit NA and exclude or impute conservatively.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Use a two-stage discrete-time hazard modeling framework. Stage A (information): Fit a complementary log-log or logistic model for received_info_t+1 with predictors: lagged fraction of informed neighbors by layer, agent fixed effects or demographics, and day fixed effects. Extract per-layer per-contact transmission probabilities (p_info_family, p_info_work_school, p_info_community) and exogenous baseline (p_info_external). Stage B (behavior): Fit a logistic model for wearing_mask_t+1 with predictors: wearing_mask_t (persistence), received_info_t, lagged neighbor_wearing_fraction by layer, risk_perception, demographics, and interactions (e.g., risk_perception × peer influence). From this, compute baseline adoption hazard (h_base), adoption uplift (Delta_info), persistence and dropout, and layer-specific peer coefficients. Optionally estimate a Bayesian hierarchical version with partial pooling across demographics to stabilize layer coefficients. Use these estimates directly as simulation parameters or translate to equivalent per-contact probabilities via contact sampling assumptions.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Perform out-of-sample temporal validation: fit on initial window (e.g., days 1–T_train), simulate forward from the observed state at T_train using calibrated parameters on the fixed network, and compare predicted vs observed trajectories on days T_train+1–T_end. Validate on: (1) population-level prevalence of wearing_mask and received_info over time (RMSE/MAE); (2) transition matrices (stay/adopt/drop rates); (3) stratified prevalence by age_group/occupation and degree quantiles; (4) peer effect diagnostics: correlation between predicted and observed adoption conditional on neighbor_wearing_fraction bins; (5) distributional checks: wearing streak lengths, time-to-first-adoption, and cascade sizes for received_info. Use posterior predictive checks if Bayesian. Sensitivity test to edge symmetrization and contact sampling assumptions.

file_summaries.semantic_summary:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Overall structure/type:
  - Flat CSV; one row per agent.
  - Primary key: agent_id (integer).
  - Field types: integers (age, connection counts), categorical strings (age_group, occupation), float in [0,1] (risk_perception), boolean (initial_mask_wearing).

- Fields and meanings:
  - Demographics: age, age_group, occupation.
  - Behavior state: initial_mask_wearing (seed adoption state at t0).
  - Psychometric: risk_perception (propensity to adopt; continuous).
  - Social degree by layer: family_connections, work_school_connections, community_connections; total_connections (intended sum of the three).

- Relationships/nested elements:
  - No nested/relational structures present; data are agent-level attributes only.
  - Implied multilayer social network via connection counts; total_connections should equal the sum of layer-specific counts (validate/recompute if needed).
  - No explicit edges or neighbor identities; network topology must be generated from degree counts (e.g., configuration model) and optionally homophily (age_group, occupation).

- How to inform simulation entities/interactions:
  - Agent initialization:
    - Set each agent’s state: mask_wearing = initial_mask_wearing.
    - Assign attributes: risk_perception, age_group, occupation for heterogeneity in thresholds/influence.
  - Network construction:
    - Build a multilayer graph with three layers: family, work/school, community.
    - Use the per-layer degree counts as target degrees for stub-matching; ensure total degree consistency across agents per layer.
    - Optionally bias edge wiring by homophily (same age_group/occupation) and enforce role constraints (e.g., Students receive work/school ties; retirees fewer).
  - Interaction dynamics:
    - Influence/update rules use:
      - Neighbor mask-wearing fraction per layer with layer-specific weights (e.g., family > work > community).
      - Agent risk_perception to modulate adoption probability/threshold.
      - Demographics to adjust susceptibility/influence (e.g., Students higher work/school exposure).
    - initial_mask_wearing seeds early adopters for diffusion.
  - Metrics:
    - Track adoption over time overall and by layer/demographic; degree distributions derived from connection counts.

Semantic metadata summary for social_network.json

Overall data structure and type
- JSON object (dictionary) keyed by agent IDs as strings (e.g., "0", "1"). IDs map to integer node IDs; range appears to be 0–999.
- Each value is an object containing four adjacency lists: family, work_school, community, and all. Elements are integer IDs of other agents.
- The all list is the union of the three context-specific lists (may contain duplicates in source; treat as a set).

Relationships or nested elements
- Multiplex network: three explicit relationship layers (family, work/school, community) representing tie types/contexts.
- Edges are stored as per-node adjacency lists; reciprocity (undirected symmetry) is not guaranteed and may need enforcement or acceptance as directed ties.
- No edge weights or timestamps; tie strength is implied by context only.
- Possible overlaps across layers (an alter could be both family and co-worker), though not evident in the sample; do not assume disjointness.
- Variable degree per layer; community lists tend to be larger, family smaller.

How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
- Agents: one per node ID. State includes mask-wearing status (binary or probabilistic), susceptibility/threshold, and possibly context-specific behaviors.
- Interaction topology: use the three layers to schedule contacts and influence. Weight contact frequency or influence strength by layer (e.g., family > work/school > community).
- Dynamics:
  - Use all for aggregate peer influence when context is not modeled explicitly; otherwise sample interactions per layer according to a daily/weekly schedule.
  - Choose a diffusion model (e.g., independent cascade with context-specific transmission probabilities, or threshold model with layer-weighted neighbor adoption).
- Preprocessing: convert keys to ints; de-duplicate neighbors; optionally enforce undirected edges; precompute neighbor sets per layer and degrees for efficiency.
- Seeding and interventions: select initial adopters and apply context-targeted policies (e.g., workplace mandates) by altering layer-specific adoption probabilities or exposure schedules.
- Metrics: track adoption over time overall and by layer/degree; examine cascade size and layer contributions.

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv

Overall data structure and type
- Format: CSV (sample shown as JSON records for readability)
- Granularity: panel/longitudinal time series at daily resolution
- Schema:
  - day: integer (time index)
  - agent_id: integer (entity identifier)
  - wearing_mask: boolean (agent behavioral state)
  - received_info: boolean (agent information/exposure state)
- One row per agent per day; no nested fields

Relationships or nested elements
- Flat schema with a composite key (agent_id, day)
- Temporal dependency within agent trajectories (state at day t influences day t+1)
- Two binary state variables per agent:
  - received_info may act as a precursor/modulator for wearing_mask adoption
  - wearing_mask can switch over time even without received_info (as in sample), indicating baseline adoption/abandonment dynamics
- No explicit social network structure included; edges/contacts must be provided elsewhere or synthesized

How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
- Agents: nodes with two binary states: wearing_mask and received_info
- Time step: daily updates
- Initialization: set initial states from earliest day per agent
- Dynamics/calibration:
  - Estimate transition probabilities:
    - P(received_info_t+1 | received_info_t, exogenous factors)
    - P(wearing_mask_t+1 | wearing_mask_t, received_info_t, possibly neighbor influence)
  - Capture baseline adoption/abandonment (when received_info = false) and the uplift when received_info = true
- Interactions:
  - Information diffusion process: received_info propagates over the social network (not in file; define/generate network and contagion rules)
  - Behavioral contagion: wearing_mask adoption influenced by own prior state, info state, and neighbors’ states
- Validation: compare simulated panel outputs to observed trajectories (marginal rates over time, persistence, switching rates, and conditional effects of received_info)
